name: Long takes
definition: Shots held well beyond conventional length, letting action unfold without a cut.

name: Static camera
definition: The camera rarely or never moves; composition does the work.

name: Tracking shots
definition: Elaborate travelling camera movement through space, on dolly, crane or Steadicam.

name: Handheld camera
definition: Visibly unstabilised camera that follows the actors closely.

name: Deep focus
definition: Foreground and background both sharp, so staging in depth replaces cutting.

name: Symmetry and frontality
definition: Centred, frontal or one-point-perspective compositions.

name: Wide-angle lenses
definition: Short lenses that exaggerate depth and distort space.

name: Expressive close-ups
definition: Faces, hands or objects in close-up carry the meaning of the scene.

name: Zooms
definition: Visible zooming in or out as an expressive device.

name: Subjective point of view
definition: The camera takes a character's optical viewpoint.

name: Widescreen composition
definition: Staging built for the full width of a scope frame.

name: Montage
definition: Meaning produced by the collision or association of shots rather than by continuity.

name: Jump cuts
definition: Cuts that break continuity within a scene and draw attention to themselves.

name: Elliptical editing
definition: Key events are skipped or left off screen; the viewer fills the gaps.

name: Cross-cutting
definition: Alternating between parallel lines of action to build tension or contrast.

name: Slow pacing
definition: Duration and stillness are foregrounded; little happens per minute by design.

name: Rapid cutting
definition: Short average shot length and percussive editing rhythm.

name: Slow motion
definition: Slowed or step-printed motion used for emphasis.

name: Pop music cues
definition: Existing pop, rock or soul songs used as a structural element.

name: Sparse soundtrack
definition: Little or no score; silence and ambient sound dominate.

name: Classical music
definition: Existing classical repertoire used in place of an original score.

name: Voice-over
definition: Narration that comments on, or runs against, the image.

name: Expressive sound design
definition: Sound effects and off-screen sound carry narrative or atmosphere.

name: Overlapping dialogue
definition: Several characters speak at once, as in real conversation.

name: Non-professional actors
definition: Roles cast with people who are not trained actors.

name: Deadpan performance
definition: Flat, withheld delivery; emotion is suppressed rather than displayed.

name: Improvisation
definition: Scenes developed with the actors rather than fixed in the script.

name: Ensemble casts
definition: Many characters of similar weight instead of a single protagonist.

name: Stylised dialogue
definition: Speech that is conspicuously written: verbose, laconic or rhythmic.

name: Theatrical staging
definition: Tableau framing, stage-like blocking or open acknowledgement of theatre.

name: Non-linear structure
definition: Events presented out of chronological order.

name: Dream logic
definition: Surreal or oneiric sequences not marked off from reality.

name: Self-reflexivity
definition: The film points at its own making or addresses the viewer.

name: Episodic structure
definition: Loose chains of episodes instead of a tight causal plot.

name: Genre revision
definition: Popular genres reworked, mixed or turned against their conventions.

name: Ambiguity
definition: Central questions are deliberately left unresolved.

name: Memory and subjective time
definition: Past, present and imagination interpenetrate.

name: Suspense construction
definition: The viewer knows more or less than the characters, by design.

name: Everyday life
definition: Ordinary routines and small events are the subject.

name: Black comedy
definition: Violence, death or cruelty played for uneasy laughter.

name: Documentary hybrid
definition: Fiction and documentary methods are mixed.

name: Stylised colour
definition: Saturated or schematic colour used expressively.

name: High-contrast lighting
definition: Strong light and shadow shape the image.

name: Natural light
definition: Available light and minimal artificial lighting.

name: Location shooting
definition: Shot in real streets, homes and landscapes instead of sets.

name: Studio artifice
definition: Visibly designed, constructed worlds.

name: Landscape and weather
definition: Terrain and weather act as a dramatic force.

name: Frames within frames
definition: Doorways, windows, mirrors and buildings structure the composition.

name: Stylised violence
definition: Violence choreographed and aestheticised.

name: Planimetric framing
definition: Camera set square to a flat background, figures arranged like a frieze.

name: Telephoto lenses
definition: Long lenses that flatten space and observe from a distance.

name: Following shots
definition: The camera travels behind or beside a walking character for extended stretches.

name: Distant framing
definition: Action staged in long shot; the camera declines to move in.

name: Off-screen space
definition: Important action happens outside the frame and is heard or implied.

name: Direct address
definition: Characters look into or speak to the camera.

name: Conversation-driven scenes
definition: Long dialogue scenes are the main event rather than a bridge between actions.

name: Freeze frames
definition: The image is stopped to punctuate or end a scene.

name: Dead time
definition: The shot continues before or after the action, dwelling on empty space or waiting.

name: Collage
definition: Stills, text, tinting, animation or found footage are cut into the film.

name: Chapters and intertitles
definition: The film is openly divided into titled parts.

name: Two-part structure
definition: The film breaks in the middle into two halves that mirror or answer each other.

name: Multiple perspectives
definition: The same events are told from competing or shifting viewpoints.

name: Journey structure
definition: A road trip or aimless wandering replaces a goal-driven plot.

name: Chamber drama
definition: A few characters confined to one or two interiors.

name: Melodrama
definition: Heightened emotion, social constraint and suffering, taken seriously.

name: Essay form
definition: Argument and reflection organise the film more than story does.

name: Child's perspective
definition: The world is seen at the level of a child protagonist.

name: Film quotation
definition: Other films are openly quoted, reworked or paid homage to.

name: Absurd humour
definition: Dry or surreal comedy that arises from routine and incongruity.

name: Provocation
definition: Taboo material or attacks on the viewer's comfort are a deliberate strategy.

name: Crowd choreography
definition: Large groups are staged as a single moving composition.

name: Mirrors and reflections
definition: Mirrors, glass and reflections double or split the characters.

name: Period reconstruction
definition: Historical settings recreated with dense, deliberate detail.

name: Musical numbers
definition: Song and dance staged for the camera as part of the film's structure.

name: Effects-driven spectacle
definition: Optical, mechanical or digital effects are central to the film's appeal.

name: Animation
definition: Images drawn, modelled or manipulated frame by frame.

name: Action choreography
definition: Fights, chases and stunts designed and filmed so that movement itself tells the story.

name: Direct observation
definition: Documentary filmed as events unfold, without narration, interviews or staging.

name: Interview and testimony
definition: The film is built from people recounting events to the camera.

name: Abstraction
definition: Light, texture, rhythm or the film material itself take the place of story.
